title: A changed herdr field is loud: strict decode of required fields
description:
Make a changed herdr field LOUD. This is the highest-value robustness tick in
the epic: a silent rename does not degrade the system, it inverts a safety
property.

Every method decodes into a fixed struct with stock encoding/json, so an added
field is dropped and a RENAMED field becomes a zero value with no error. Four
are load-bearing, all in AgentInfo:

- `agent_status` renamed -> "" -> IsTerminal false (wait.go:67-74) -> the wave
  never fans in -> a 30-second fan-in becomes a 30-minute hang (wait.go:55).
- `interactive_ready` renamed -> always false -> readiness always exhausts its
  deadline (spawn.go:440-446) -> EVERY spawn fails as a startup race.
- `name` renamed -> nil -> reconcile's liveNames map is empty
  (reconcile.go:192-196) -> every live worker classifies as dead -> REDISPATCH
  ONTO A TICK THAT ALREADY HAS A RUNNING WORKER, which reconcile.go:96-98 names
  as the invariant it must never break.
- `agent_session` renamed -> nil -> workers classify as non-resumable and
  recovery silently downgrades from native resume to redispatch.

Do:
- Required fields are REQUIRED: decoding a response that omits one is a typed
  error naming the method and the field, never a zero value. Decide and log
  whether that is `DisallowUnknownFields`-style strictness, explicit presence
  checks with pointers, or a validate step; unknown ADDED fields must stay
  tolerated (forward compatibility) while missing required ones must not.
- An unknown agent status is an explicit error, not silently non-terminal. This
  alone is the difference between a 30-minute hang and a clear refusal.
- One bad event must not kill the stream: today a single decode failure ends it
  (events.go:508-511). Skip the event, record it, keep the subscription.
- Stop swallowing: `resultType` discards its unmarshal error
  (client.go:243-249); spawn.go:304 discards an AgentGet error while
  back-filling agent_session, making a failed lookup indistinguishable from an
  agent that has none.

2026-09-10 15:53 - Contract deviation to fix at integration: the worker committed RESULT-bcv.md (122 lines) onto tick/bcv. Every other worker in this epic left it untracked, which is what tk herd cleanup expects — archive to .tick/logs/herd/av8/, then remove. The only precedent for a committed report is cc5, whose entire deliverable WAS the report. Drop the file from the merge and archive it normally. The systemic fix is recorded on tick d9m: the herdr executor must enforce the artifact boundary the way Phase 1's subprocess executor does — a git exclude written before the agent starts, plus an independent branch-diff check at collect that refuses AND reports a force-added report. .tick/learnings.md already states the rule from an earlier incident: a boundary the substrate can enforce must not rest on instruction-following.
acceptance_criteria: A response missing a required field is a typed error naming method and field, never a zero value; an added unknown field is still tolerated; an unknown agent status is an explicit error rather than silently non-terminal; a decode failure on one event skips that event and keeps the stream; the resultType and AgentGet error swallows are gone; tests cover each of the four load-bearing renames (agent_status, interactive_ready, name, agent_session) and assert the failure is loud rather than a zero value; go test -short -timeout 45m ./... green.
closed_reason: Strict decode of herdr's load-bearing fields: a new ~290-line module with 460 lines of tests, plus client, events and protocol changes. Its new tests were verified to fail at the base commit a085b31, which is the check this epic learned to demand. Deviation noted and corrected at integration: it committed RESULT-bcv.md onto its branch; archived and removed. Wave gate green (EXIT=0, reconcile 710s).
